translation.title: Ketoconazole Cream
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for skin fungal infections: ringworm (ringworm of the body, jock itch and athlete's foot), skin candidiasis, pityriasis versicolor and seborrheic dermatitis.
translation.usage: Usually apply once a day, or twice a day depending on the severity of the infection. Keep applying it for several days even after the symptoms have disappeared.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine if you are hypersensitive to it, on a wounded or inflamed scalp, or on severely eroded (raw, oozing) areas. Before using it, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if you are breastfeeding, for children, or if you are or have been hypersensitive to propylene glycol. In the case of candidiasis, do not use acidic soap. Do not use an occlusive dressing or wrapping unless directed by a doctor. This medicine is for external use only. Do not use it in the eyes; apply it carefully so that it does not touch the eyes, and if it accidentally gets into the eyes, rinse them out completely with plenty of water. When using this medicine together with antifungals of the same class (such as miconazole, econazole or isoconazole), consult a doctor or pharmacist. Adverse reactions may occur at the application site, such as occasional contact dermatitis, a rash, a burning feeling of the skin, skin peeling, blistering rash, sticky skin, hypersensitivity, redness, itching, dryness, irritation, bleeding, discomfort, inflammation or abnormal sensations, and very rarely hives, pain or a burn; if they occur, stop use and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
